featuredStory.title: Exhibit 1: William Lane of Boston
featuredStory.subtitle: Opening the Lane story in chronological order
featuredStory.summary: William Lane of Boston (cordwainer) anchors the opening exhibit: Hartford and Lynn appearances, freeman 1657, and the Mary Brewer marriage — chronology that later Lanes extend from.
historianNotes: Book narrative cites Hist. Gen. Reg. XII, 196 for harmonizing Hartford (Samuel b. 8 Aug. 1648) and Lynn (1651); verify against NEHGR and town records.
First church Boston, Mary’s death 1656, second marriage to Mary Brewer (Roxbury) — use as baseline before Stratham and later migrations.

citations.label: NEHGR — New England Historical and Genealogical Register (vol. 12 context; see XII:196 in book)

prominentLanes.caption: Opening exhibit · colonial New England chronology anchor (William E. / William Lane merged)
prominentLanes.blurb: Some records may be harmonized if William Lane were residing in Hartford, Connecticut, where he had a son, Samuel, born 8 August 1648, and visiting in Lynn in 1651 [see Hist. Gen. Reg. XII, 196]. He was made freeman 6 May 1657. His wife Mary, a member of the first church in Boston (probably from England), died 22 May 1656; and he married (2) 21 August 1656, by Richard Bellingham, Deputy Governor, to Mary (daughter of Thomas) Brewer of Roxbury, Massachusetts. Her father, Goodman Brewer, in 1642 resided in Ipswich, removed afterward to Roxbury, and died at the home of his son-in-law, Thomas Webster, in Hampton, 3 March 1689–90.
